**1 — Scene:** A breakfast tray with toast, fried eggs, banana, orange juice, and a small yogurt tub. I include both plates and the drink and yogurt on the same tray.

**2 — Vessels:** Main plate approximately **26 cm** across: area **531 cm²**. Banana side plate approximately **20 cm**: **314 cm²**. The glass and yogurt tub are estimated separately.

**3 — Items:** Two slices of toast, two fried eggs, one peeled banana, orange juice, and yogurt. No separate butter or sauce is clearly visible; frying fat is included in the eggs’ energy estimate.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Vessel area covered | Area × average height = volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Toast, two slices | 38% of main plate | 202 cm² × 1.1 cm = 222 ml | 0.30 g/ml¹ | 67 g | 268 | 180 kcal |
| Fried eggs, two | 28% of main plate | 149 cm² × 0.65 cm = 97 ml | 0.98 g/ml | 95 g | 196 | 186 kcal |
| Banana | 22% of side plate | 69 cm² × 1.5 cm = 104 ml | 0.90 g/ml | 93 g | 89 | 83 kcal |
| Orange juice | Glass interior | Average 28 cm² × 9 cm = 252 ml | 1.03 g/ml | 260 g | 45 | 117 kcal |
| Yogurt | Tub interior, inferred | 28 cm² × 5 cm = 140 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 140 g | 65 | 91 kcal |

¹Toast uses a porous bread bulk density, with no additional reduction for air. Banana is treated as dense whole fruit rather than loosely piled pieces.

**Area check:** Toast and eggs cover approximately **66%** of the main plate; banana covers approximately **22%** of its plate. These match the substantial exposed plate areas.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **655 g and 660 kcal** is plausible for this breakfast, including the juice and yogurt. Yogurt quantity and type are particularly uncertain because the tub is opaque and its label is not fully readable.
